title: Spending Northbeam Renew Trade-In Credit and the Sweep at the End of Its Life
content:
Issued Northbeam Renew Trade-In credit is spent at face value against merchandise, and never against tax, delivery, dues or a protection plan premium. The smallest amount that may be spent at once is the Renew programme's minimum, and where the programme does not allow partial spending the whole credit is spent in one transaction or not at all. Credit is spent only by the profile it was issued to, unless the programme allows transfer, in which case it moves once and the new holder inherits the expiry day. Credit still unspent at the end of its validity days is written off in the sweep for that year and is never restored, and an expiry is never reversed as a courtesy. Where a purchase paid for with credit is returned, the credit is put back with the expiry day it originally carried rather than a fresh one.

**What the credit may and may not meet.**

| Put against | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| merchandise | yes, at face value |
| tax | no |
| delivery | no |
| dues | no |
| a protection plan premium | no |

**Spending it in parts.** Where the programme allows partial spending, an amount at or above the programme's minimum may be drawn at a time. Where the programme does not allow partial spending, the whole credit is spent in one transaction or not at all; there is no middle course.

**Transfer.** The credit stays with the profile it was issued to unless the Renew programme allows transfer. Where transfer is allowed it moves once, and the profile it moves to takes the expiry day the credit already carried rather than a fresh one.

**The sweep and a return.** Credit unspent when its validity days run out is written off in that year's sweep, and it is not restored afterwards, nor is an expiry reversed as a courtesy. Where a purchase that was paid for with credit is returned, the credit comes back carrying the expiry day it originally had.
